title: Early Sepsis Detection Using NEWS2 and Circulating H3.1 Nucleosomes in Emergency Departments
official: Real-life Evaluation of the Impact of Early Detection of Sepsis With the NEWS2 Clinical Alert Score Combined to Circulating Concentrations of the H3.1 Nucleosome, on the Care Pathway of Adults Presenting to the Emergency Department With a Proven or Strongly Suspected Infection
summary:
DETECSEPS is a multicentre, randomized, open-label trial sponsored by Assistance Publique - Hôpitaux de Paris, under the scientific leadership of IHU SEPSIS - PROMETHEUS Comprehensive Sepsis Center, led by Professor Djillali Annane.

The study evaluates whether an early sepsis detection strategy combining the National Early Warning Score 2 (NEWS2) and circulating H3.1 nucleosome concentrations improves care pathways compared with usual care in adults presenting to emergency departments with suspected or confirmed infection and at least one risk factor for sepsis.

The strategy aims to support timely recognition and management of sepsis and to identify patients suitable for discharge with ambulatory follow-up when hospital admission is not otherwise indicated. The study will assess care pathway optimization at 24 hours, clinical outcomes, health-related quality of life, return to usual activities, and economic and environmental outcomes.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria

1. All genders patients
2. Aged of 18 years or older
3. Proven or suspected infection
4. At least one risk factor for sepsis (cf HAS recommendations) :

   * Age/frailty : \>65 year; Clinical Frailty Scale ≥5; postpartum; Cognitive or motor disabilities; Implantable medical device; Recent surgery
   * Inborn immune deficit
   * Acquired immune deficit :

     * Diseases related : Cancer, Transplant patient, Chronic inflammatory or autoimmune disease, HIV, Asplenic anatomical or functional (Sickle cell disease)
     * Treatment related : Long-term corticotherapy, chemotherapy, Biotherapy, Cell therapy, radiotherapy, Immunosuppressive drugs,
   * Non immune disorders : Cirrhosis, chronic liver disease, chronic renal insufficiency, chronic cardiac failure, diabetes with complication or uncontrolled, malnutrition, previous episode of sepsis
5. Informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Refused to consent participating in the study,
2. Any condition for which patient's primary physician will consider inappropriate enrolling patient in the study,
3. Previous enrolment
4. Pregnancy
